honesty.banner: Curated structural industry baseline — not a live breaking-news feed. Threats, opportunities, and Takes are labeled analysis or structural context. Live activations appear separately when evidence-backed impacts are available.
honesty.confidenceRules: Observed is reserved for established facts. Predictive threats, opportunities, and citizen-impact hops must never use Observed. Missing or invalid confidence defaults to Unknown.
honesty.analysisRules: Waypoint’s Take is analysis and interpretation — never established fact. Do not treat curated baseline text as verified live intelligence.
honesty.liveRules: Live developments load from live-impacts.json when present. Missing or empty live impacts must show an honest empty state — never invent activations.

crossLinks.notes: Country Intelligence, Citizen Impact category deep-links, and Relationship Explorer may ship on parallel branches. Soft-link with stable IDs (gsc_*, gsci_*, gsa_*, gsi_*). Articles routes exist on main.

industries.name: Semiconductors
industries.tagline: Foundries, tools, and chip design sit at the center of modern industry.
industries.summary: Semiconductors concentrate design, fabrication equipment, specialty chemicals, and advanced packaging into a small set of geographies and firms. Capacity, export controls, and water/energy constraints shape what other industries can ship.

whatIsHappening.text: Leading-edge logic capacity remains concentrated in a few foundries, while governments fund domestic fabs and tighten export controls on advanced tools and chips. Packaging, specialty gases, and EUV tool supply remain tight relative to demand for AI and automotive silicon.

why.text: Chips are an intermediate good for nearly every modern product. When lithography tools, photomasks, or advanced packaging nodes bottleneck, Automotive, Technology, Healthcare devices, and Defense electronics feel delayed availability long before consumers see a headline about ‘chips.’

threats.label: Geographic concentration of advanced fabs
threats.detail: A small number of sites produce most leading-edge logic; natural disaster, conflict, or energy disruption at those sites would cascade widely.

threats.label: Export-control friction
threats.detail: Licensing regimes on tools and advanced nodes can slow technology transfer and re-route supply graphs without eliminating demand.

threats.label: Water and power intensity
threats.detail: Fabs require reliable ultrapure water and stable power; drought or grid stress can constrain utilization.

opportunities.label: Mature-node capacity for autos and industrial
opportunities.detail: Not every chip needs the newest node; expanding mature capacity can ease Automotive and industrial shortages.

opportunities.label: Advanced packaging and chiplets
opportunities.detail: Heterogeneous integration can stretch existing silicon and create new assembly hubs.

opportunities.label: Diversified specialty chemical routes
opportunities.detail: Alternate chemical and gas suppliers reduce single-point failure in fab inputs.

Diversification of mature nodes and packaging can reduce some citizen-facing scarcity without solving geopolitics. industries.name: Energy
industries.tagline: Fuels, grids, and generation that power every other industry.
industries.summary: Energy links extraction, refining, pipelines, shipping, electricity generation, and grids. Cyber incidents, weather, and corridor security can move fuel and power availability faster than most other sectors.

whatIsHappening.text: Oil and gas still set much of transport and industrial heat cost, while power grids absorb rising electrification and data-center load. Pipeline cyber risk, maritime corridor diversions, and weather extremes remain recurring stress tests for fuel and electricity reliability.

why.text: Energy is the universal intermediate. When pipelines pause, tankers divert, or grids strain, Transportation, Shipping, Food cold chains, Construction materials, and households feel cost or reliability pressure.

threats.detail: IT/OT incidents can pause physical flows even when malware targets billing systems.

threats.label: Grid congestion and extreme weather
threats.detail: Heat, cold, or storms can force load shedding or price spikes regionally.

opportunities.detail: Batteries and demand response can dampen short spikes without new baseload overnight.

opportunities.label: Efficiency in industry and buildings
opportunities.detail: Lower intensity reduces exposure to fuel shocks.

opportunities.detail: Multiple pipelines, LNG terminals, and interconnectors reduce single chokepoints.

industries.name: Agriculture
industries.tagline: Crops, livestock, fertilizers, and weather-sensitive production.
industries.summary: Agriculture converts land, water, fertilizer, seed, and labor into commodities that feed Food processing and trade. Weather, ports, and fertilizer energy costs are recurring transmission channels.

whatIsHappening.text: Yields and planting decisions remain highly weather-dependent, while fertilizer costs track energy and export policies. Port and canal constraints affect export crop schedules; labor and water stress shape regional production capacity.

why.text: Agriculture is the upstream of Food. Disruptions in fertilizer, water, or export corridors show up later as Food prices and Availability of goods — with long lags and many offsets.

industries.name: Transportation

industries.summary: Transportation connects ports, farms, factories, and cities. Fuel availability, vehicle components (including semiconductors), and labor determine how Shipping and Retail shocks propagate inland.

whatIsHappening.text: Freight networks absorb port queues and corridor diversions through trucking and rail. Fuel price sensitivity and vehicle component lead times continue to shape capacity. Passenger travel costs track fuel and schedule reliability.

why.text: Without inland Transportation, Shipping arrivals and Agriculture harvests do not become Retail inventory. Fuel and labor are the binding constraints that turn distant events into local delays.

why.text: Most intercontinental trade still travels by sea. A chokepoint delay is a multi-industry delay — Logistics in article tags often means this layer.
